v.why: Large batches give few, low-noise steps in a fixed epoch budget, so a higher lr relieves undertraining without the noise that destabilizes small-batch runs.
Deeper stacks compound Adam's per-parameter updates, moving the divergence cliff to lower lr.
Wide layers sum many Adam updates so the function-space step grows with width and crosses the instability threshold earlier.
Tiny batches add gradient noise on top of many updates, so a smaller lr restores stability where the lr is otherwise too high.
At low lr training is step-limited, so fewer updates from a larger batch deepen undertraining.
Averaging more samples tames the gradient noise that drives high-lr Adam into divergence.
When lr is tiny, more updates per epoch from smaller batches directly relieve undertraining.
Moving from already-strong L2 (0.129 to 1) to stronger L2 over-regularizes and collapses weights, unlike the harmless small-alpha regime.
Penalty is normalized per batch so small batches feel an effectively stronger L2, and raising alpha there tips into underfitting.
Depth supplies missing capacity for narrow nets that cannot get it from width.
High lr compounds across extra layers into exploding or dead ReLU activations.
Strong L2 shrinks every layer so the product of weights collapses multiplicatively with depth.
At low lr extra layers increase function-space movement per step and speed up otherwise undertrained fits.
With a single hidden layer width is the only capacity route, so it pays off most there.
At low lr wider layers move further in function space per step and avoid undertraining.
With few steps from large batches, wider nets fit faster per update and compensate for the small step count.
Pushing an already high lr (0.08 to 1) goes past the divergence cliff, while from lower bands it helps or is neutral.
Raising a tiny lr (1e-5 to 1e-4 range) cures severe undertraining in 243 epochs, a gain unavailable elsewhere.
Backing off from a divergent or chaotic lr recovers accuracy, whereas lowering lr in mid or low bands is neutral or harmful.
With per-batch-normalized L2 a large batch weakens the effective penalty, so raising alpha is milder and can add useful regularization.
